notes.what_this_is: Known supervisory validation breaks and coverage holes, ratcheted by tests/acceptance/reporting/test_supervisory_validations.py. An entry is a LIABILITY, not a waiver: an ERROR-severity break rejects the entire return at submission.
notes.how_to_read_a_reason: Each entry names the DEFECT, not the symptom. A reason beginning 'unattributed - needs investigation' means the mechanism is written out but the cause is not established - it is a lead, not a shrug.
notes.caution_on_unattributed: 'Unattributed' can mean the question was framed too narrowly, not only that the evidence is thin. Worked example: boe_b0378 was recorded as 'c0060 is a signed outflow column, so of-which <= total inverts' - a real-looking question whose answer was neither limb offered, because the total should never have been negative at all (the carrier was uncapped, upstream of the sign question). Re-derive the framing before trusting an unattributed entry's framing.
notes.caution_on_arithmetic_coincidence: Do not read an arithmetic coincidence as evidence of a mechanism. boe_b0752_22/24 were once attributed to a class-level figure being 'broadcast' onto every PD-grade row, on the evidence that the grade sum was exactly 7x the total across 7 grades. That is equally consistent with a genuine per-grade average whose inputs coincide - which is what it was. The decisive evidence was float dust (1672.9999999999995 on one row of seven): a broadcast constant would be bit-identical.
notes.caution_on_plan_doc_definitions: A plan document naming a column as the DEFINITION of a basis is not evidence the column implements it. Worked example: docs/plans/phase7-declarative-reporting.md's F3 decision (the Pillar 3 CR4/CR5 tranche) cites 'C 07.00 col 0200 basis' as what 'post-substitution' MEANS - it assumed col 0200 already carried that basis, not that it should. That assumption was false at the time and broke v0308_m/boe_b0471/v8726_m/boe_b0556: C 07.00's own col 0200 summed EAD over the ORIGIN population (the F4 build never extended substitution-awareness to it), while CR4/CR5 (reporting/pillar3/cr4.py, cr5.py) keyed the post-substitution `reporting_class` they cite the same definition for - so two parts of the estate that cite one shared basis were inconsistent. RESOLVED: C 07.00 col 0200/0220 (and the C 08.01 / C 09.02 cousins) were rebound to the post-substitution population, col 0200 now reads Sum(ead_col) over that basis, and the four rules were removed from this register. Retained as the lesson: verify a definition is IMPLEMENTED before citing it as evidence a related gap is a deliberate decision rather than a build shortfall.
notes.pattern_boe_summation_templates: The BoE summation rules do not distinguish ADDITIVE columns from AVERAGED ones. 'r0070 = sum(grade rows)' is applied across all ~36 columns of OF 08.01/08.02, including exposure-weighted averages, where it cannot hold unless there is exactly one grade row. Same shape as boe_b0779 on c0050 and v09782_m/v09783_m on C 08.06's risk-weight column. Recognise it before re-deriving it a fourth time.
notes.pattern_empty_subrow_vs_negated_column: An inequality between an 'of which' sub-row and its parent inverts when the parent is a genuinely negative Annex II Sec.1.3 '(-)' deduction column and the sub-row's own subset is empty: our empty-subset convention renders the sub-row ALL-NULL, the evaluator coalesces that null to 0.0 for the comparison, and 0 <= a negative number reads false however correct that negative figure is. Same shape as the zero-exposure ratio family (boe_b0778/v09782_m and boe_b0779's 'no emptiness guard' — see the caution on unattributed entries above before assuming the parent's negative figure is itself the bug, as it genuinely was in the boe_b0378 worked example there).

known_broken_rules.reason: known limitation of the published rule, not a defect in our output (notes.pattern_empty_subrow_vs_negated_column): row 0017 ('of which: revolving loan commitments') has zero population on this fixture (no revolving product is modelled) and renders structurally null under the empty-subset convention; the evaluator coalesces that null to 0.0 for the comparison. The failing columns (0040/0050/0070) are the Annex II Sec.1.3 '(-)' substitution-block deduction columns, which we report NEGATIVE and non-zero for the first time on any portfolio (this is the first guarantee outflow the estate has ever exercised). VERIFIED not the notes.caution_on_unattributed trap (a prior boe_b0378 case where the negative total was itself an uncapped-carrier bug): c0040's -12,300,000 is exactly the sum of the three 'guarantee'-type legs' covered amounts (S1 2,000,000 + S3 4,900,000 + S5 5,400,000 = 12,300,000, per tests/fixtures/reporting_crm_substitution_portfolio.py), and c0050's -3,300,000 is exactly S2's 'credit_derivative' covered amount - both figures are correct. The inequality is written for positive magnitudes: on a negative Total it inverts, so 0.0 <= a genuinely negative (and correct) figure reads false. Same mechanism as boe_b0379 (row 0200 vs row 0190, identical coordinates and figures)

unattributed - needs investigation: OF 07.00 c0150 carries on-balance-sheet exposure while cols 0160-0190 break down conversion-factor buckets, so the identity cannot hold on any row with on-BS exposure. BOTH sides recorded, because the reading is textual and NOT established. Against us: PS1/26 Annex II p.85 qualifies c0150 as 'prior to the application of any applicable conversion factors' - a PRE-CCF qualifier, not an off-balance-sheet-only one - and the very next block spends the words 'of off-balance sheet items' exactly where c0150 does not, which reads as deliberate. For us: the EBA equivalent v6364_m is scoped to row 0080 alone and PASSES for us, while the BoE scope carries 26 rows including r0010 TOTAL. Needs a regulatory reading, not a code change

limit of the published rule, not of our output: c0230 and c0250 are exposure-weighted AVERAGES, and summing an average down the 7 PD-grade rows cannot equal the class-level average unless there is exactly one grade row (0.4 against 2.8; 1,673 against 11,711). Our per-grade values are correctly computed, not broadcast: c0110 differs on every grade row, and c0250 carries float dust on one of the seven (1672.9999999999995), which a broadcast constant could not. They coincide only because every corporate leg in this fixture shares the same supervisory F-IRB LGD and maturity. See notes.pattern_boe_summation_templates

limit of the published rule, not of our output: the exposure-weighted RESTATEMENT of boe_b0752_22 / boe_b0752_24, and it fails for exactly the same reason. The weighting factor is identical on both sides - b0756 multiplies both by (sum(c0110) - sum(c0140)), b0758 both by sum(c0110) - so it cancels and the rule reduces to the same 'class average = sum of grade averages' assertion. Verified arithmetically: b0756's 20,440,000 vs 143,080,000 is 0.4 vs 2.8 scaled by 51,100,000, and b0758's 85,490,300,000 vs 598,432,100,000 is 1,673 vs 11,711 scaled by the same. NB the rule LOOKS like it intends the correct paired identity - each grade's average times that grade's own exposure - but as published it multiplies two separate sums, which the simplified expression cannot express as a per-grade pairing. Either reading leaves it unsatisfiable against a correct return. See notes.pattern_boe_summation_templates

limit of the published rule, not of our output: after the DPM-fraction fix these now fail ONLY on roll-out-class rows with ZERO exposure, where every coordinate reads lhs=0.0 against rhs=1.0. A row with no exposure admits no partition - 0/0 has no answer - and the rule carries no emptiness guard, so it demands the three shares total 1 on a row where there is nothing to share. Coordinate counts now vary by portfolio (6-14 CRR, 3-7 B3.1) purely with how many roll-out classes each leaves empty

limit of the published rules, not of our output: boe_b0779 and boe_b0778 CONTRADICT each other on c0050 and cannot both hold. b0778 requires the three share columns 0030/0040/0050 to total 1 on each row; b0779 requires row 0260 to equal the sum of rows 0180-0250 - but c0050 is a RATIO, so summing it down eight roll-out rows cannot equal the total row's own ratio (0.868 against 2.068). The instruction text resolves in b0779's favour on scope: row 0260 sums rows 0180-0250 'for each of columns 0060-0150', and c0050 is not in that set, so the rule should never have reached this column. We report the ratio; the single remaining coordinate is c0050 alone

OF 09.01 r0095 c0010 (geographic breakdown, original exposure pre-CCF) reports 825,000.00 where OF 07.00 sheet 0010 r0020 c0010 reports 0.00. Cross-template class-row mapping defect between the geographic breakdown and the SA template: one side attributes the real-estate split's secured leg to a class row the other leaves empty. PRE-EXISTING and newly REACHABLE, not newly broken -- it fires identically on the unfixed engine, and became visible only when the re-split and funded-protection portfolios were registered in RUNS. WARNING severity, so it does not reject a submission. Filed as a plan item; not caused by the carrier-conservation batch.

As boe_b0990 on the exposure-value axis: OF 09.01 r0095 c0075 reports 825,000.00 against OF 07.00 sheet 0010 r0020 c0200 at 0.00. Same cross-template class-row mapping defect, same pre-existing-and-newly-reachable status (fires on the unfixed engine), WARNING severity. Filed with boe_b0990 as one item -- the three are one defect seen on three columns, so they must be fixed and un-banked together.

As boe_b0990 on the RWEA axis: OF 09.01 r0095 c0090 reports 495,000.00 against OF 07.00 sheet 0010 r0020 c0220 at 0.00. Same cross-template class-row mapping defect, pre-existing (fires on the unfixed engine), WARNING severity. The RWEA is 60% of the exposure value, consistent with an Art. 124L residual leg at the counterparty weight, which is a hint at where the mapping diverges. Filed with boe_b0990/0991 as one item.
